source.title: Beyond Symmetric Alignment: Spectral Diagnostics of Modality Imbalance in Vision-Language Models in the Medical Domain
source.authors: Alessandro Gambetti; Qiwei Han; Cláudia Soares; Hong Shen

record.tranche_reason: The study measures image-text alignment across datasets, metrics, and SAS settings, and reports that the measured alignment and directional imbalance depend on those choices. It does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The reported model zoo includes models from approximately 150M to over 1B parameters, but the study does not report alignment as a function of size or model capability. It measures alignment across natural and medical datasets, compares metrics, and sweeps the SAS quantile parameter. Retrieval results are not rows here because they measure downstream retrieval rather than representation alignment.
record.test_reason: The study measures how well the image and text encoders of the same contrastively trained dual-encoder VLM align on paired data, across natural vs medical datasets, metrics and the SAS q parameter. This alignment is built in by the joint contrastive objective. It is not convergence between independently trained models, and the study does not relate it to model scale or capability. Per the gating rules, this is a related but different construct with the behaviour induced on purpose. None of the originals are cited or tested. The only nod to convergence is one sentence saying CKA/SVCCA suit checking whether architectures converge.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors conclude medical images carry richer structure than paired reports can recover. They also find SAS is the strongest label-free predictor of retrieval in the medical domain (Spearman 0.969). They present cosine margin and SAS as complementary diagnostics, and note q needs domain-specific calibration.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces and evaluates a new asymmetric spectral alignment metric and compares it with existing metrics; it does not reproduce either original source's convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: Alignment scores and domain gaps vary with dataset/domain, metric choice, and SAS quantile q. The study reports RMG as an exception to the domain-shift result; it also reports different ΔSAS magnitudes across ROCO and MIMIC-CXR and across medical VLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-text alignment within general-purpose contrastive VLMs drops from natural (COCO, Flickr30k) to medical (ROCO, MIMIC-CXR) data on 9 of 10 metrics. RMG is the exception (p=0.179), and CORAL moves the other way.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Built-in cross-modal alignment of contrastive dual encoders degrades under domain shift, and whether this is detected depends on the metric.

fits_no_version.finding: Directional ΔSAS is ~0 on natural data but positive on medical data. On ROCO it is positive for every model (+0.082); on MIMIC-CXR it is smaller (+0.015).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Contrastive VLMs show a modality information imbalance (image over text) on medical data.

fits_no_version.finding: SAS scores and the natural-medical gap shrink as more eigenmodes are included (q 0.1→1.0). Medical ΔSAS grows to +0.062 at q=0.7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral alignment scores depend on eigenspectrum depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Of the medical VLMs, PubMedCLIP aligns much more than PLIP on ROCO (CKA 0.623 vs 0.181). Both have near-zero MIMIC-CXR retrieval.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-specific pretraining varies in its effect on cross-modal alignment, and alignment is not sufficient for retrieval.

record.problems: The benchmark is limited to four datasets and a finite model zoo; the study reports no scale- or capability-conditioned alignment analysis. The authors state that SAS requires equal feature dimensions, that q requires domain-specific calibration, and that alignment alone does not ensure retrieval performance. Some aggregate metric results show substantial variation, particularly for medical data.
record.rows_left_out: No additional alignment results were omitted. Retrieval correlations and retrieval scores were left out because they measure downstream retrieval rather than representation alignment.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models and no alignment vs scale or capability, even though the zoo spans ~150M to 1B+ parameters.
Image and text towers are jointly trained within each model. No independently trained vision and language models, and no trend with model quality.
No cross-model mapping, stitching or relative representations.
Metric, domain and q dependence are studied only for within-model image-text alignment, not for cross-model convergence.
No test of plateau or of shared data/objective as causes of cross-model convergence.

record.verdict_notes: The reader labeled this as a V6 test. I re-gated it: every alignment measured is between a single model's jointly contrastively trained image and text encoders. That is a designed-in objective, not emergent convergence of independently trained models, and the study never engages the Platonic or convergent-learning claims. All rows are relinked to none; findings are recorded under fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: No reported relationship between increasing model size/capability and alignment between independently trained models.
Image-text paired data are measured, but the study does not test whether alignment increases as both modalities' models improve.
No comparison of same-architecture models trained from different seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are tested.

The study tests metric, dataset/domain, and SAS quantile dependence in its medical and natural image-text benchmark; it does not test other choices such as neighbour count or out-of-distribution generalization beyond these domains.
The study does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain convergence, or whether cross-model convergence plateaus.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Natural versus medical datasets in the general-purpose VLM benchmark
reader_labels.reason: Most reported metrics differ significantly across domains, and the directional ΔSAS result is near zero on natural data but positive on medical data; see r1–r4, r7–r20.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Changing q changes the scores and domain gap; the text reports changing ΔSAS and a monotonic decrease in directional scores as more modes are included; see r25–r29.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Metric-specific and dataset-specific results, including RMG and medical datasets
reader_labels.reason: RMG does not significantly distinguish natural from medical data, and the per-dataset and medical-model results show different magnitudes and directional patterns; see r5–r6 and r21–r33.
